reasoning_traces.think:
The framework employs a latent changepoint chain to model discrete regime shifts in multivariate time series. Each activity is segmented into latent states governed by a block-diagonal Gaussian state-space model. The doubly-online nature allows for both retrospective and real-time inference. The model assumes linear-Gaussianity and fixed design matrices, limiting adaptability to complex or non-stationary environments. The key innovation lies in the use of sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) for approximate Bayesian inference, enabling scalable changepoint detection in streaming data. Failure modes include over-segmentation due to aggressive threshold δ=0.5, computational inefficiency for long sequences, and lack of flexibility in modeling non-linear dynamics or time-varying covariates. The framework's strength resides in its ability to detect subtle shifts in athlete health metrics, but its application to NFL data requires careful calibration of changepoint priors and validation of convergence properties on shorter time series.
